key_insight: SoundnessBench shows that frontier LLMs are still unreliable at judging whether a research idea is methodologically sound, with a strong tendency toward optimistic false positives.
engineering_relevance: For AI research agents, this means automated idea screening cannot yet serve as a dependable first gate for scientific rigor without human oversight.
method: Built SoundnessBench from 1,099 ML research proposals reconstructed from ICLR submissions.
Labeled proposals using reviewer soundness sub-scores and audited them against source papers.
Benchmarked 12 frontier LLMs under standard and aggressive prompting, plus confounder controls.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluates recoverable proposal-stage soundness rather than full-paper review outcomes, using 1,099 proposals and 12 LLMs to measure bias and error shifts.
watch_item: Because the dataset is reconstructed from submissions and reviewer scores, results may not generalize perfectly to all scientific domains or real-world proposal workflows.
paper_title: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
